title: Turf Bar and Jack Johnson's place
summary: Sitting in at the Turf Bar and playing out on Eight Mile Road with pianist Johnny Van, who played to a dead sweetheart's pictures.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: And a friend of mine...well, one of the guys from home who had played Don Dunbar's orchestra, Simon(?) Jefferson, he invited me to play...to come down and play with him on his gig at a place on St. Antoine, just below Adams in Detroit, called the Turf Bar. And they had one of those bandstands behind the bar, high bandstands, you know. So I used to go down and sit in with him. So eventually, I started making myself a little name around the city. So I started getting calls on different kinds of gigs and things.

I remember one gig I played that was kind of interesting. I played out on Eight-Mile Road at Jack Johnson's, the ex-heavyweight champion's place, and he was like the host. And we had a very fine group there. I was working with a drummer named Johnny Johnston, and the piano player who played with him was an excellent pianist Johnny Van(?). Johnny Van was quite a guy. He had been deeply in love with this young lady who had passed, and he carried her pictures in his briefcase all the time, and when he would come to the job he would sit her pictures on the piano and play to her. And you never heard such soulful playing as this guy sitting there playing to this girl. It was kind of sad. But what he got out of it was something. It was really spectacular.
